dish: Shakotan uni-don — red vs purple uni side by side (Jun–Aug)
w: An uni fisherman's own shop: additive-free sea urchin landed that morning, with a ten-a-day bowl comparing bafun (red) and murasaki (purple) uni in season.

dish: additive-free Shakotan uni-don over the 'Shakotan Blue' sea
n: Shokudō Ushio, Shakotan (食堂 うしお)
w: A half-century seaside canteen buying uni straight from the fishermen and serving it untreated, with the cape's blue water out the window.

n: Oshokujidokoro Misaki, Shakotan (お食事処 みさき)
address: Near Cape Kamui, Shakotan, Shakotan District, Hokkaido, Japan
w: Fisherman-run at the tip of the peninsula — the owner is out for uni at 4am, and the limited bafun bowl sells out daily in season.

dish: year-round Otaru sake from Hokkaido rice and Mt Tengu water — free tasting
n: Tanaka Shuzō Kikkōgura, Otaru (田中酒造 亀甲蔵)
w: An 1899 brewery in a stone warehouse that brews all four seasons thanks to Hokkaido's cool climate — walk the brewery, then taste free.

dish: Otaru Beer German-style lagers brewed in the canal warehouse
n: Otaru Sōko No.1 — Otaru Beer (小樽倉庫No.1)
w: A brewpub inside a canal-side stone warehouse with the brewery on view — lagers from German organic barley and Otaru's soft water, with German-style plates.

dish: 'Hanazono dango' — rice-flour dumplings under a hand-swept wave of bean paste (since 1895)
n: Niikuraya Hanazono Honten, Otaru (新倉屋 花園本店)
w: An 1895 wagashi house whose Hanazono dango wear their red-bean paste in a single mountain-shaped sweep.

dish: cream zenzai — red beans, mochi and soft-serve
w: A Shōwa-era Otaru sweet parlour still loved for its cream zenzai.
